141	
142	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
143	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
144	
145	Add a track when you need another layer, name it so the stack stays readable, and clear out the tracks you've stopped using.
146	
147	<AtAGlance
148	  menu={['Track ▸ New Track', 'Track ▸ Remove Track', 'Track ▸ Remove Empty Tracks']}
149	  keys="⇧⌘N"
150	  where={['Double-click or drag a track header', 'Right-click a track header or an empty stretch of its lane']}
151	  tools={['add_track', 'remove_track', 'move_track', 'set_track', 'remove_empty_tracks']}
152	/>
153	
154	## New Track
155	
156	Choose **Track ▸ New Track** or press <kbd>⇧⌘N</kbd>. An empty track appears at the front, as the top lane. It's named from the track count, such as `Track 4` when there are three tracks.
157	
158	A project holds at most 64 tracks, and the tracks inside nests count towards that. Past the limit, Frame Job shows an error and adds nothing.
159	
160	## Drop past the stack
161	
162	You can make a track and fill it in one move:
163	
164	- Drag clips above the top lane to make a new front track for them.
165	- Drag clips below the bottom lane to make a new back track for them.
166	
167	Clips selected on more than one track can only make a new back track. The new track and the move are one undo step, and this works for a <kbd>⌥</kbd>-drag duplicate too. See [Move clips](/editing/move-clips/).
168	
169	Dropping a file from the Media tab on the preview also adds a new front track for it.
170	
171	## Rename a track
172	
173	<Steps>
174	
175	1. Double-click the track's header, away from its switches. A name field opens in place.
176	
177	2. Type the new name.
178	
179	3. Press <kbd>Return</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd>, or click somewhere else.
180	
181	</Steps>
182	
183	<kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the field and keeps the old name. So does clearing the field, because this field can't leave a track with no name. Spaces at either end of the name are dropped. [Clips](/timeline/names-and-labels/#rename-a-clip) and [markers](/timeline/markers/#move-rename-and-remove-a-marker) rename in the same kind of field.
184	
185	## Reorder tracks
186	
187	Drag a track's header up or down. A coral line shows where it will land, and the track moves there when you let go.
188	
189	Dragging a header changes what draws in front of what. It also changes what a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/) cuts, because a matte cuts the track directly behind it. A locked track can be moved like any other.
190	
191	## Remove Track
192	
193	**Track ▸ Remove Track** removes the [current track](/timeline/tracks/#the-current-track). **Remove Track** in the [track context menu](#the-track-context-menu) removes the track you clicked, which is how you remove an empty track that isn't the front-most, since an empty track has no clip to select.
194	
195	An empty track goes at once. A track that still holds clips asks first, in an alert titled with the track's name: "The track still holds 3 clips, which will be removed with it." Choose **Remove** or **Cancel**. One undo brings back the track and its clips.
196	
197	A project always keeps one track, so the last one can't be removed. **Remove Track** is greyed out on it in the context menu. **Track ▸ Remove Track** stays available, but Frame Job beeps and says why at the foot of the inspector. If that last track holds clips, the alert comes first.
198	
199	## Remove Empty Tracks
200	
201	**Track ▸ Remove Empty Tracks** drops every track that holds no clips, as one undo step. Hidden, locked and named tracks go too if they're empty. If every track is empty, the back-most one stays. If no track is empty, Frame Job beeps.
202	
203	## The Track menu
204	
205	The **Track** menu's commands work on the [current track](/timeline/tracks/#the-current-track), apart from **New Track** and **Remove Empty Tracks**.
206	
207	| Item | Key | What it does |
208	| --- | --- | --- |
209	| **New Track** | <kbd>⇧⌘N</kbd> | Adds an empty track at the front. |
210	| **Remove Track** | | Removes the current track. |
211	| **Remove Empty Tracks** | | Drops every track with no clips. |
212	| **Hide Video** | | Flips the current track's [Hide Video](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/#hide-video) switch. |
213	| **Mute Audio** | | Flips its [Mute Audio](/audio/mute-and-solo/) switch. |
214	| **Lock Track** | | Flips its [Lock Track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/#lock-track) switch. |
215	| **Solo** | | Flips its [Solo](/audio/mute-and-solo/) switch. |
216	| **Mix…** | | Opens its [mix panel](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/). |
217	| **Matte** | | Makes it a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/): **Off**, **Alpha**, **Inverted Alpha**, **Luma** or **Inverted Luma**. |
218	
219	Of the four switches, only **Solo** shows a checkmark in this menu, because a soloed track with nothing on it still silences the rest and you can't always hear that. For the other three, read the track's header.
220	
221	## The track context menu
222	
223	Right-click or <kbd>⌃</kbd>-click a track's header, or the empty part of its lane, to get a menu for that track:
224	
225	- **Hide Video**, **Mute Audio**, **Lock Track** and **Solo**, each checked when it's on
226	- **Mix…**
227	- **Matte**, with the track's mode checked
228	- **Remove Track**, greyed out on the last track
229	
230	Every item acts on the track you clicked, not the current track, and shows that track's own state. A right-click on a clip, the ruler or the corner above the headers opens no menu.
231	
232	## Undo names
233	
234	Every switch flip, rename and reorder is one undo step, and **Edit ▸ Undo** (<kbd>⌘Z</kbd>) names the edit it will reverse. The names for edits to tracks, markers and clip labels are:
235	
236	| Edit | Undo name |
237	| --- | --- |
238	| Track switches | Hide Track, Mute Track, Lock Track, Solo Track |
239	| A track's matte | Track Matte |
240	| A track's mix | Track Volume, Track Pan, Track Compressor, Track Limiter, Reset Track Mix |
241	| Track names and order | Rename Track, Reorder Track |
242	| Adding and removing tracks | New Track, Remove Track, Remove Empty Tracks |
243	| Markers | Add Marker, Move Marker, Rename Marker, Chapter Marker, Remove Marker |
244	| Clip names and labels | Rename Clip, Label Clip |
245	
246	## Good to know
247	
248	- With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, everything on this page works on the nest's own tracks, except that the mix panel's compressor and limiter are turned off there.
249	- **Remove Track** takes only the clips on that track. A linked picture or sound on another track stays, and is no longer linked.
250	
251	## With an agent
252	
253	[`add_track`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#add_track) can put a new track anywhere in the stack and name it as it's made, where you'd add it at the front and then drag it. [`move_track`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#move_track) moves a track to a numbered place in the stack, 0 being the back. To do what a drop past the stack does, an agent adds the track and then moves the clips onto it with [`move_clip`](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#move_clip).
254	
255	[`remove_track`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#remove_track) never asks: it leaves a track that holds clips alone unless it's told to take them too, and it won't remove the last track.
256	
257	These tools also work on the tracks inside a nest. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/) and [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).

267	description: Take a track's picture out of your video without touching its clips, and protect a track from being moved or cut by accident.
268	---
269	
270	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
271	
272	**Hide Video** takes a track's picture out of your video and leaves its clips where they are. **Lock Track** protects a track's clips while you edit everything around them.
273	
274	<AtAGlance
275	  menu={['Track ▸ Hide Video', 'Track ▸ Lock Track']}
276	  where={['The eye and padlock switches in a track header', 'Right-click a track header or an empty stretch of its lane']}
277	  tools={['set_track']}
278	/>
279	
280	## Hide Video
281	
282	Click the eye in the track's header. It becomes a struck-through eye and the track's clips draw dimmed on the timeline. Click it again to bring the picture back.
283	
284	**Hide Video** in the [track context menu](/timeline/manage-tracks/#the-track-context-menu) does the same for the track you clicked, and **Track ▸ Hide Video** for the [current track](/timeline/tracks/#the-current-track).
285	
286	While a track is hidden:
287	
288	- Its picture is gone from the preview and from every export.
289	- Its clips aren't drawn on the canvas, so you can't click them there. You can still select and edit them on the timeline.
290	- Its sound keeps playing. To silence it as well, use [Mute Audio](/audio/mute-and-solo/).
291	- A hidden [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/) cuts nothing, so the track behind it shows whole.
292	- If it holds a [nest](/editing/nests/), everything inside the nest is hidden too.
293	
294	## Lock Track
295	
296	Click the open padlock in the track's header. It closes and the lane is hatched. Click it again to unlock.
297	
298	**Lock Track** in the [track context menu](/timeline/manage-tracks/#the-track-context-menu) does the same for the track you clicked, and **Track ▸ Lock Track** for the [current track](/timeline/tracks/#the-current-track).
299	
300	### What a lock stops
301	
302	On the timeline, you can't drag, trim, slip or roll a locked track's clips with the mouse. Their trim edges are gone, and their fade handles, volume lines and action bands don't respond. A marquee skips them.
303	
304	On the preview, you can't select or drag them. A click passes through to the unlocked clip behind.
305	
306	Edits that reach across the timeline leave a locked track alone:
307	
308	- [**Split**](/editing/splitting/) with nothing selected doesn't cut its clips.
309	- [**Lift** and the range form of **Ripple Delete**](/editing/delete-clips/) leave them uncut.
310	- Ripples, [closed gaps](/editing/close-gaps/) and inserted time don't shift them. That includes the cuts from [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/).
311	- A clip on a locked track isn't moved, cut or deleted along with a linked partner on an unlocked track.
312	
313	### What Frame Job won't do
314	
315	A few edits need to shift or cut a locked track to work, so Frame Job stops them.
316	
317	| Edit | What happens |
318	| --- | --- |
319	| [Insert](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/) onto a locked track | Beeps and says why at the foot of the inspector. |
320	| [Close Gap](/editing/close-gaps/) on a locked track | Beeps and says why at the foot of the inspector. |
321	| [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) | Won't run while a locked track has a clip that ends after the range's start, because that clip would fall out of step. |
322	
323	### What a lock doesn't stop
324	
325	A lock protects where a clip sits, not what it looks like. You can still rename a clip on a locked track and change it in the inspector.
326	
327	You can also still select one by clicking it on the timeline, with <kbd>⌥</kbd>-click on the header, or with **Edit ▸ Select All on Track**. Once a locked clip is selected, the edits you aim at it still work:
328	
329	- **Delete** and **Ripple Delete** remove it.
330	- **Split** cuts it.
331	- **Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead** (<kbd>W</kbd>) and **Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead** (<kbd>E</kbd>) trim it.
332	- <kbd>,</kbd> and <kbd>.</kbd> nudge it along the timeline.
333	- If you drag an unlocked clip in the same selection, the locked clip moves with it.
334	
335	A few other things get past a lock too:
336	
337	- [**Overwrite**](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/) still clears the span it needs on a locked track.
338	- You can drop a clip or a file onto a locked track.
339	- You can [reorder](/timeline/manage-tracks/#reorder-tracks) or [remove](/timeline/manage-tracks/#remove-track) a locked track.
340	- [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) cuts locked tracks like any other, and the new project keeps their locks.
341	
342	## Good to know
343	
344	- Each flip is one undo step, named Hide Track or Lock Track.
345	- **Track ▸ Hide Video** and **Track ▸ Lock Track** show no checkmark, so read the state from the track's header. The context menu does show one.
346	
347	## With an agent
348	
349	`set_track` sets both switches, as `hidden` and `locked`. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#set_track).
350	
351	A lock holds back gestures in the window and edits that reach across the timeline. As with a clip you've selected, an agent that names a clip on a locked track can still move, trim, cut or delete it. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/).
352	
353	## Related
354	
355	- [Tracks](/timeline/tracks/)
356	- [How edits work](/editing/how-edits-work/)
357	- [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/)
358	- [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/)

360	title: Track height
361	description: Choose small, medium or large track rows, and see how a track's contents and the row size change what a clip shows.
362	---
363	
364	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
365	
366	Track height sets how tall the timeline's rows are. Go small to see more tracks at once, or large to get more room for filmstrips, waveforms and actions.
367	
368	<AtAGlance
369	  menu={['View ▸ Timeline Track Height ▸ Small', 'View ▸ Timeline Track Height ▸ Medium', 'View ▸ Timeline Track Height ▸ Large']}
370	  where="The S / M / L control at the right end of the timeline bar"
371	/>
372	
373	## Small, Medium, Large
374	
375	Click **S**, **M** or **L** at the right end of the timeline bar, or choose a size from **View ▸ Timeline Track Height**. The menu checks the size you're on.
376	
377	Medium is the default. Your choice is remembered between launches and applies to every project, because it's a view setting and not part of the project. It makes no undo step, and no agent tool sets it.
378	
379	## Height follows contents
380	
381	A track's height also depends on what it holds, so sound-only and text tracks draw shorter than picture tracks.
382	
383	| Track holds | Small | Medium | Large |
384	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
385	| Only text and shapes | 30 pt | 44 pt | 58 pt |
386	| Only clips with sound and no picture | 40 pt | 60 pt | 82 pt |
387	| Anything else, an empty track included | 54 pt | 84 pt | 116 pt |
388	
389	The row changes as the track's contents do. A music track grows to picture height when you drop a video on it, for example. An adjustment clip, a graphic or a nest counts as picture.
390	
391	A clip's own switches count. A detached sound, with its picture off, is a clip with sound and no picture.
392	
393	## What each size shows
394	
395	Every clip keeps its 16 pt name strip, and the rest of the row goes to its filmstrip, its waveform and its actions. So at Small a clip shows little more than its name: 8 pt is left under the strip on a text row, 18 pt on a sound row and 32 pt on a picture row.
396	
397	The action lane under the name strip changes with the size:
398	
399	| Size | Lane height | Each action band shows |
400	| --- | --- | --- |
401	| Small | 5 pt | A plain bar. |
402	| Medium | 12 pt | Its number in time order, and a zoom glyph for a zoom action. |
403	| Large | 18 pt | The same, plus the properties it changes. |
404	
405	See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/) for what each part of a clip means.
406	
407	## Good to know
408	
409	- A size change applies to the window you made it in. Other windows that are already open keep their size, and the next one you open uses your latest choice.
410	- While you drag a clip, lanes keep their heights, so the track you're aiming at doesn't move under the pointer. They settle when you drop.
411	
412	## Related
413	
414	- [Tracks](/timeline/tracks/)
415	- [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/)
416	- [Zoom and scroll the timeline](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/)
417	---
418	title: Reading a clip on the timeline
419	description: What every colour, symbol, line and handle on a clip block means, so you can read a timeline without selecting anything.
420	---
421	
422	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
423	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
424	
425	A clip on the timeline tells you what it is, what it holds and what's been done to it, without being selected. This page is the key to those marks. Each mark's control has its own page, linked from here.
426	
427	<AtAGlance where="The timeline's lanes" tools={['set_selection', 'set_audio']} />
428	
429	<Shot
430	  name="04-editor.window"
431	  alt="The editor with four tracks on the timeline: a green audio clip with its fade handles and a white volume line, two teal clips for a shape and a graphic, and an amber text clip. Each clip has its name in a darker strip along the top with a small symbol for its kind, and the playhead runs through every track."
432	/>
433	
434	## The clip block
435	
436	Each clip draws as one block with 2 pt rounded corners and a thin border, so you can always see where one clip ends and the next begins.
437	
438	From top to bottom, a block holds its name strip, its action lane if it has actions, its filmstrip and its waveform. The filmstrip sits under a tint of the clip's own colour and the waveform is drawn on that colour, so a clip reads as one coloured object rather than a row of photographs.
439	
440	The action lane shows a band for each [action](/motion/action-lane/). The selected action's span is also tinted down the whole height of the clip, in the action colour: mint in dark mode, a deeper green in light mode.
441	
442	## Colour by kind
443	
444	A clip's colour and the symbol on its name strip tell you its kind.
445	
446	| Kind | Colour | Symbol |
447	| --- | --- | --- |
448	| Video | Slate | A strip of film |
449	| Audio | Green | A waveform |
450	| Image | Violet | A photo |
451	| Freeze frame | Violet | A snowflake |
452	| Text | Amber | Letters |
453	| Shape | Teal | A square on a circle |
454	| Graphic | Teal | Curly braces |
455	| Nest | Grey | A stack of squares |
456	| Adjustment | Rose | Overlapping filter circles |
457	
458	The kind comes from what the clip shows, not only from its file. A video file's clip with its picture switched off reads as audio, in green with the waveform symbol. That's how the sound half of a [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) pair looks.
459	
460	A [label](/timeline/names-and-labels/) never changes the block's colour, because the colour says what the clip is and a label is something you said about it.
461	
462	## The name strip
463	
464	The darker strip along the top of a clip carries, from left to right, its kind symbol, a link symbol if it's [linked](#linked-clips), its name, a wave if it has a During motion, and its label dot.
465	
466	A clip with a name of its own shows that. Otherwise it shows what it holds: a nest's name, the file's name, the text itself, or the shape's kind. A clip with none of those reads as its kind, such as **Graphic** or **Adjustment**. A name too long for the strip ends in an ellipsis.
467	
468	On a narrow clip the strip leaves out what won't fit. The kind symbol stays longest, and the dot and the wave are left out when they'd run into the symbols.
469	
470	### The label dot
471	
472	A labelled clip shows a small dot in its label colour at the right end of the name strip. See [Clip names and labels](/timeline/names-and-labels/).
473	
474	### Motion marks
475	
476	Two small marks show a clip's active [motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/):
477	
478	- **A wedge** along the bottom of the name strip, from the left end for an In preset and from the right end for an Out preset. It's as long as the preset's duration at the current zoom, and it rises towards its inner end, so you can see how far into the clip the motion runs. It's never shorter than 2 pt or wider than the clip.
479	- **A small wave** at the right end of the strip, to the left of any label dot, for a During movement.
480	
481	## Picture and sound
482	
483	Below the name strip, a clip shows what it holds: its picture as a filmstrip, its sound as a waveform, or both.
484	
485	### Filmstrip
486	
487	Thumbnails run along the picture part of a video or image clip, each 34 pt wide and cropped to fill its tile.
488	
489	A file's strip holds one frame for each second, so a thumbnail shows that point in the clip to within a second or so. It follows the clip's trims, speed, reverse and speed ramps. A filmstrip of a log file with a [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) set, or of an HDR file in PQ or HLG, shows the converted picture, matching the preview, not the flat image in the file.
490	
491	The strip covers the first 600 seconds of a file. Later in a longer file, the clip shows its plain colour.
492	
493	An image has one thumbnail, so only the first second of an image clip shows it. A freeze frame's strip starts at the moment it froze.
494	
495	Text, shape, graphic, nest and adjustment clips have no thumbnails.
496	
497	### Waveform
498	
499	A clip with sound draws it as a waveform, below the filmstrip when the clip has both. The waveform follows the clip's source time through speed changes and ramps. A nest clip draws no waveform, even when it has sound.
500	
501	The waveform draws faded when the clip or its track is muted, or when another track's solo silences it. A track's mute button stays unlit under another track's solo, so the waveform is the place to look to see what's in the mix. See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/) and [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/).
502	
503	### Filling in after import
504	
505	Filmstrips and waveforms are made once for each file and kept with the project, so they fill in a moment after you add a file. See [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/).
506	
507	## Lines over a clip
508	
509	Up to four thin lines show how a clip changes over time, and each has its own control.
510	
511	### The volume line
512	
513	A thin white line over the waveform shows the level you hear from the clip, with its volume, fades, ducking and volume actions folded in. The top of the audio part is +30.1 dB and the bottom is −60 dB, and a silenced clip's line lies along the bottom. Small squares in the action colour mark where a volume action ends.
514	
515	Nest clips don't draw it. To change the level from the timeline, see [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/).
516	
517	### The duck line
518	
519	A thin yellow line over a clip set to duck by speech shows where the rest of the mix goes down and comes back. The top of the audio part is the mix at full level and the bottom is silence.
520	
521	A duck set to **Clip Length** draws no line, because it lasts as long as the clip. See [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/).
522	
523	### The Hide While Silent line
524	
525	A teal line across the picture part of a clip with [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) on shows where the clip fades out in each pause and back in before speech. The top is fully shown and the bottom is fully hidden. The line appears once Frame Job has analysed the speech in the file the clip follows.
526	
527	### The rate line
528	
529	A clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) draws its rate as a white line with a dark edge across its action lane, here and in the Clip tab's lane. The bottom of the lane is the clip's own slowest rate and the top its fastest, so a small ramp looks as tall as a big one. Read the numbers in the Speed section.
530	
531	The timeline draws it at the Medium and Large [track heights](/timeline/track-height/), not at Small.
532	
533	## Fade handles
534	
535	Small white squares at the top corners of a clip's audio part set its fades. Drag one inward to fade in or out. The square sits at the corner with no fade, and at the end of the fade once there is one.
536	
537	The fade's length snaps to whole frames and stops at the clip's length. It doesn't snap to clip edges. The handles write the same two values as the Fades section, so see [Audio fades](/audio/fades/) for the rest.
538	
539	## The transition zone
540	
541	The overlap between two clips draws as a hatched zone with a solid edge down each side. The transition's kind is written in it when the whole word fits. On a short transition the word is left out, and the [Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/) still names it. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).
542	
543	## Selected clips
544	
545	A selected clip gets a 2 pt coral ring, and most commands act on it. When the clip is wide enough to trim and its track is unlocked, it also shows a [trim](/editing/trimming/) grip at each end. See [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/).
546	
547	## Linked clips
548	
549	A picture and the sound Detach Audio split from it each show a link symbol after their kind symbol. Select one and the other gets a dashed ring in your Mac's accent colour, because moving one moves both. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
550	
551	## Dimmed clips
552	
553	A clip draws dimmed when its track is hidden, or when both its picture and its sound are switched off. A muted clip isn't dimmed. Only its waveform fades.
554	
555	## Adjustment clips
556	
557	An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) is a plain rose block with only its name strip and action lane. It has no filmstrip or waveform, and its track is as tall as a picture track.
558	
559	## Good to know
560	
561	- A short track leaves marks out. The filmstrip needs 10 pt of height, the waveform, duck line and Hide While Silent line 8 pt, the fade handles 10 pt and the volume line 12 pt. A text clip at the Small [track height](/timeline/track-height/) is little more than its name strip.
562	- A [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) draws a faint hatch across its whole lane, over its clips. Clips on it show no trim grips, and their fade handles don't drag.
563	- On a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), clips draw at half strength with a dashed outline.
564	- Inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/), a Hide While Silent line that follows a file outside the nest stays flat along the top, though the clip still fades.
565	
566	## Related
567

574	title: The ruler and playhead
575	description: Read the timeline's time ruler, scrub along it, and see how the playhead decides where edits land.
576	---
577	
578	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
579	
580	The ruler is the strip of time above the tracks. The playhead marks one moment on it: the frame the preview shows, and the point where most edits land.
581	
582	<AtAGlance where="The ruler above the timeline's tracks" tools="set_playhead" />
583	
584	## The playhead
585	
586	The playhead is the coral line down every track, with a triangle head on the ruler. A click or a drag lands it on a frame.
587	
588	## Scrub on the ruler
589	
590	Click the ruler to move the playhead there, and drag along it to scrub. Pressing on the ruler pauses playback, and it stays paused when you let go.
591	
592	While you scrub, you hear the sound under the playhead. The press plays a short piece of it, and the drag plays more as it reaches new frames. See [Hear a scrub](/audio/scrub-audio/).
593	
594	The scrub [snaps](/timeline/snapping/) like any other drag. Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> to scrub without snapping.
595	
596	A press within 6 pt of a marker's line grabs the [marker](/timeline/markers/), not the ruler, so start the scrub beside it.
597	
598	## Lane clicks
599	
600	A click in a lane doesn't move the playhead. On empty space it starts a [marquee selection](/timeline/selecting-clips/), and a plain click there clears the selection.
601	
602	The exception is a click on an [action band](/motion/action-lane/), which moves the playhead to the end of that action so the preview shows its end state.
603	
604	## The edit point
605	
606	These commands work at the playhead, so put it where you want the edit first:
607	
608	| Command | Key |
609	| --- | --- |
610	| [**Clip ▸ Split**](/editing/splitting/) | <kbd>⌘T</kbd> |
611	| [**Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead**](/editing/trimming/#trim-to-the-playhead) | <kbd>W</kbd> |
612	| [**Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead**](/editing/trimming/#trim-to-the-playhead) | <kbd>E</kbd> |
613	| [**Clip ▸ Freeze Frame**](/speed/freeze-frame/) | <kbd>⇧⌘F</kbd> |
614	| [**Edit ▸ Paste**](/editing/copy-and-paste/) | <kbd>⌘V</kbd> |
615	| [**Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead**](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/) | No key |
616	| [**Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead**](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/) | No key |
617	| [**Mark ▸ Add Marker**](/timeline/markers/) | <kbd>M</kbd> |
618	
619	To place the playhead exactly, [step by frames](/timeline/playback/#step-frames) or [jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/).
620	
621	## Ticks and labels
622	
623	The ruler's ticks adapt to the zoom. Zoomed in, they mark single frames. As you zoom out, they step through 2, 5 and 10 frames, then 1, 2, 5, 10, 15 and 30 seconds, then 1, 2, 5, 10, 15 and 30 minutes, and at the widest one hour.
624	
625	Labels use the project's timecode format, **Frames** or **Milliseconds**, set in [the Document tab](/projects/background-and-timecode/). A timeline under an hour long drops the leading `00:` from its labels so they fit.
626	
627	The ruler also carries [markers](/timeline/markers/), the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) and the selected [action's](/motion/action-lane/) span. Inside an open [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/), it counts from the nest's own start and shows no markers.
628	
629	## Following the playhead
630	
631	The timeline scrolls itself to keep the playhead in view, during playback and after a jump. When the playhead comes within 24 pt of either edge of the visible part, or leaves it, the view moves so the playhead sits about a third of the way in.
632	
633	## With an agent
634	
635	[`set_playhead`](/mcp/tools-view-state/#set_playhead) moves the playhead and the preview, in silence. It isn't an edit, so there's nothing to undo. An agent that splits, freezes a frame or adds a marker without giving a time works at the playhead. See [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/).
636	
637	## Related
638	
639	- [Play, pause and shuttle](/timeline/playback/)
640	- [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/)
641	- [Zoom and scroll the timeline](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/)
642	- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
643	- [Hear a scrub](/audio/scrub-audio/)

645	title: Play, pause and shuttle
646	description: Play the timeline with Space, shuttle it at up to four times speed with J, K and L, and step it frame by frame.
647	---
648	
649	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
650	
651	Play the timeline to watch your edit. It all runs from the keyboard: <kbd>Space</kbd> plays and pauses, <kbd>J</kbd>, <kbd>K</kbd> and <kbd>L</kbd> shuttle forwards or backwards at up to four times speed, and the arrow keys step to the frame you want.
652	
653	<AtAGlance
654	  keys={['Space', 'J', 'K', 'L', '←', '→', '⇧←', '⇧→']}
655	  where="The Play and Pause button in the toolbar"
656	  tools="set_playhead"
657	/>
658	
659	## Play and pause
660	
661	Press <kbd>Space</kbd>, or the Play button among the toolbar's transport buttons. The button shows Play or Pause to match, and it stays in the same spot. There's no menu item for it.
662	
663	<kbd>Space</kbd> works from wherever the focus is in the window, with a few exceptions:
664	
665	| Where you are | What <kbd>Space</kbd> does |
666	| --- | --- |
667	| Typing in a text field, the Text tab's text area, the canvas text editor or the Media tab's search field | Types a space. Typing ends with <kbd>Return</kbd>, <kbd>Tab</kbd> or a click outside the field, and <kbd>Space</kbd> plays straight after. |
668	| On the preview canvas | Plays or pauses when you let go, because the press gets ready to [pan](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/). If you panned while holding it, letting go does nothing. |
669	| On a button, pop-up or segmented control focused with Full Keyboard Access | Presses that control. |
670	| With a sheet open | Doesn't play or pause. |
671	
672	<kbd>⇧Space</kbd> plays and pauses too. Any other modifier leaves the key alone. Holding <kbd>Space</kbd> down doesn't toggle playback over and over.
673	
674	## J, K and L
675	
676	<kbd>L</kbd> plays forward, <kbd>J</kbd> plays in reverse and <kbd>K</kbd> pauses.
677	
678	| Press | What happens |
679	| --- | --- |
680	| <kbd>L</kbd> or <kbd>J</kbd> while stopped | Plays at ×1 in that direction. |
681	| The same key again | Steps up from ×1 to ×2 to ×4. At ×4 it stays at ×4. |
682	| The opposite key | Goes straight to ×1 in that direction. |
683	| <kbd>K</kbd> | Pauses. |
684	
685	These keys also work from the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-keys/) and the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/). They don't work while you're typing in a field or while a sheet is open.
686	
687	## Step frames
688	
689	<kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd> pause playback and move the playhead one frame. With <kbd>⇧</kbd>, they move ten. This is the way to place a cut exactly.
690	
691	Stepping is silent, unlike a [scrub on the ruler](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/#scrub-on-the-ruler). In the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-keys/), these keys move by word instead.
692	
693	To go further in one press, see [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/).
694	
695	## At the end
696	
697	Playback stops at the end of the timeline, and the playhead stays there. Press <kbd>Home</kbd> to [go back to the start](/timeline/move-the-playhead/). With [Loop](/timeline/loop/) on, playback goes back to the start of the loop instead.
698	
699	An empty timeline has nothing to play, so Play, <kbd>J</kbd> and <kbd>L</kbd> beep.
700	
701	## After an edit
702	
703	You can edit while the timeline plays. What you notice depends on what you changed.
704	
705	### Look-only edits
706	
707	A change that only alters how something looks, such as a clip's position, a colour or some text, redraws the frame in place. Playback isn't interrupted.
708	
709	### Structural edits
710	
711	A move, a trim, a new clip or anything else that changes the timeline's shape makes Frame Job rebuild what the preview plays, in the background. So does a change to the sound, such as volume, pan or the compressor. It keeps your place and keeps playing at the same speed. While you drag, the rebuild waits until you pause briefly.
712	
713	### Failed rebuild
714	
715	If a rebuild fails, Frame Job shows the error and the previous version of the timeline keeps playing.
716

726	title: "Jump around the timeline"
727	description: "Move the playhead straight to the next cut, either end of the timeline, or a time you type."
728	---
729	
730	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
731	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
732	
733	These are the quick ways to put the playhead where you want it: hop from cut to cut, go to either end of the timeline, or type a time. To drag it along the ruler, see [The ruler and playhead](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/). To step frame by frame, see [Play, pause and shuttle](/timeline/playback/). To hop between flags, see [Markers](/timeline/markers/).
734	
735	<AtAGlance
736	  keys={['↑', '↓', 'Home', 'End']}
737	  where={['The transport buttons in the toolbar', 'The timecode field in the toolbar']}
738	  tools="set_playhead"
739	/>
740	
741	## Jump between edit points
742	
743	Press <kbd>↑</kbd> for the previous edit point and <kbd>↓</kbd> for the next. The **Previous Edit Point** and **Next Edit Point** buttons either side of Play in the toolbar do the same.
744	
745	An edit point is the start or end of any clip, on any track, and the two ends of the timeline.
746	
747	- <kbd>↑</kbd> with nothing earlier goes to the start of the timeline.
748	- <kbd>↓</kbd> on the last edit point stays where it is.
749	- Playback keeps going. The playhead jumps and plays on from there.
750	- With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, these step through the nest's clips.
751	
752	## Go to the start or end
753	
754	Press <kbd>Home</kbd> for the start of the timeline and <kbd>End</kbd> for the end, or use the **Go to Start** and **Go to End** buttons, on the outer side of the edit point buttons. Both pause playback first.
755	
756	The keypad's Home and End work too, and so does the <kbd>fn</kbd> key with <kbd>←</kbd> or <kbd>→</kbd> on a keyboard without them. With a nest open, they go to the start and end of the nest.
757	
758	## Type a time to jump
759	
760	The toolbar shows the playhead's time in a field. You can type into it.
761	
762	<Steps>
763	
764	1. Click the time.
765	
766	2. Type where you want to go.
767	
768	3. Press <kbd>Return</kbd> or <kbd>Tab</kbd>, or click somewhere else in the editor.
769	
770	</Steps>
771	
772	Playback pauses, the playhead moves to the nearest frame, and the keys go back to the editor, so <kbd>Space</kbd> plays straight away.
773	
774	The field takes any of these, whichever way the project displays time. You can leave out leading zeros, so `1:05` and `01:05` mean the same.
775	
776	| You type | Example | It means |
777	| --- | --- | --- |
778	| Hours, minutes, seconds and frames | `00:01:23:12` | 1 minute 23 seconds and 12 frames |
779	| Hours, minutes and seconds with milliseconds | `00:01:23.500` | 1 minute 23.5 seconds |
780	| Hours, minutes and seconds | `1:23:04` | 1 hour 23 minutes 4 seconds |
781	| Minutes and seconds | `1:23` | 1 minute 23 seconds |
782	| Seconds with a decimal | `83.5` | 83.5 seconds |
783	| A bare number of seconds | `83` | 83 seconds |
784	
785	Text that isn't a time beeps, and the field goes back to the playhead's time. Only whole numbers count as frames, so `00:00:01:12.5` isn't a time.
786	
787	A leading minus sign is accepted, but the playhead can't go before the start, so a negative time lands on the first frame.
788	
789	The field shows frames by default. The [Document tab's **Timecode** row](/projects/background-and-timecode/) switches it to milliseconds, along with the duration beside it, the ruler and the times in the **Clip** and **Document** tabs. The field stops following the playhead while you type in it.
790	
791	## Read the duration
792	
793	After the time, the toolbar shows a slash and the length of what the timeline shows, such as `/ 00:00:05:07`. It's written the same way as the time, in frames or milliseconds.
794	
795	With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, both numbers are the nest's: the time counts from the nest's own start, and the duration is the nest's length.
796	
797	## Good to know
798	
799	- Moving the playhead is never an edit. It makes no undo step, and it isn't saved with the project.
800	- When a jump lands outside the visible part of the timeline, the view scrolls to bring the playhead back.
801	- With the text of the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-keys/) in focus, the arrow keys move through its words.
802	- None of these keys work while you're typing in a field or while a sheet is open. They do work in the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/).
803	
804	## With an agent
805	
806	[`set_playhead`](/mcp/tools-view-state/#set_playhead) moves the playhead to a time and seeks the preview. It doesn't pause playback. [`split`](/mcp/tools-cut-and-delete/#split), [`freeze_frame`](/mcp/tools-speed/#freeze_frame) and [`add_marker`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#add_marker) use the playhead when they're given no time. See [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/).
807

816	title: "Loop playback"
817	description: "Repeat a passage of the timeline while you watch and adjust."
818	---
819	
820	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
821	
822	Loop keeps playback going round, so you can watch a passage over and over while you adjust it.
823	
824	<AtAGlance where="The Loop button in the toolbar" />
825	
826	## Turn Loop on
827	
828	Click **Loop**, the repeat button at the end of the transport in the toolbar. The button is dimmed while Loop is off and at full strength while it's on. Click it again to turn Loop off.
829	
830	Loop has no menu item and no key. It's off when a window opens, each window has its own setting, and it isn't saved with the project.
831	
832	## What it repeats
833	
834	| What's set | What Loop repeats |
835	| --- | --- |
836	| An [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) | The range |
837	| No range, or a range of no length | The whole timeline, going back to its start and stopping there |
838	
839	With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the whole timeline means the whole nest. Entering or leaving a nest clears the range.
840	
841	The loop follows as things change. Set a new in or out point, clear the range or change the timeline's length while Loop is on, and the next pass uses the new span.
842	
843	## How playback goes round
844	
845	When playback reaches the end of the loop, it jumps back to the loop's start and carries on, at [×2 and ×4](/timeline/playback/#j-k-and-l) as well.
846	
847	A loop that ends at the very end of the timeline is different, and that includes the whole timeline. Playback jumps back to the loop's start and stops there, so press play to go round again. To keep going round, set the out point before the end of the timeline.
848	
849	- Press play at or past the end of the loop and it starts again from the loop's start.
850	- Press play before the start of the loop and it plays from where the playhead is. It only jumps back once it reaches the loop's end.
851	- Loop only works forwards. Playing backwards with <kbd>J</kbd> doesn't go round, and carries on past the start of the loop.
852	
853	## Good to know
854	
855	- The **Preview** button in the [**Motion presets**](/motion/motion-presets/) section, and **Clip ▸ Motion ▸ Preview**, set the in/out range to the clip and turn Loop on. Both stay that way until you clear the range and turn Loop off.
856	- Selecting words in the Transcript tab sets the range, so Loop plays those words. See [Follow along and jump](/captions/follow-the-transcript/).
857	
858	## Related

2	title: "Zoom and scroll the timeline"
3	description: "Zoom the timeline out to see a whole project or in to single frames, and scroll along it."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	Zoom the timeline out to see a whole project at once, or in to place a cut on a single frame. Everything on this page changes the timeline only. To zoom the picture, see [Zoom and pan the preview](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/).
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu="View ▸ Fit Timeline"
12	  keys="⇧Z"
13	  where={['The zoom controls at the right of the timeline bar', 'Pinch, or ⌥ or ⌘ and scroll, over the timeline']}
14	/>
15	
16	## Zoom about the pointer
17	
18	Put the pointer on the part of the timeline you care about, then either:
19	
20	- pinch on a trackpad, or
21	- hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> or <kbd>⌘</kbd> and scroll.
22	
23	The time under the pointer stays where it is while everything else spreads out or closes in around it, which makes this the best way to get close to one cut.
24	
25	## Use the zoom slider
26	
27	Drag the **Timeline Zoom** slider in the timeline bar. It zooms about the middle of the view, and it covers the whole zoom range on a log scale, so the same travel always changes the zoom by the same ratio.
28	
29	## Step with the zoom buttons
30	
31	The **Zoom Out** (−) and **Zoom In** (+) buttons sit either side of the slider. Each click moves the zoom by 5 % of the slider's travel, which is about 1.6 times, and keeps the middle of the view in place. Twenty clicks cross the whole range.
32	
33	## Fit the whole project
34	
35	Press <kbd>⇧Z</kbd>, click **Fit Timeline** (the double-arrow button after the + button), or choose **View ▸ Fit Timeline**. The whole project fits across the timeline pane and the view scrolls to the start.
36	
37	The menu item shows no key, because <kbd>⇧Z</kbd> is one of the keys the editor handles itself. This is the only timeline zoom with a menu item or a key.
38	
39	A project under 1 second long fits as if it were 1 second. With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, Fit Timeline fits the nest.
40	
41	:::note
42	**View ▸ Zoom In**, **Zoom Out** and **Zoom to Fit** zoom the preview, not the timeline.
43	:::
44	
45	## How far it zooms
46	
47	A window opens with each second of the timeline 42 points wide on screen, not fitted to the project, so press <kbd>⇧Z</kbd> to see all of a long project. A point is the unit macOS measures the screen in.
48	
49	The zoom runs from 0.35 points per second, where an hour is 1,260 points wide, to 4,000 points per second, where one frame of a 30 fps project is about 133 points wide. It stops at either limit.
50	
51	The zoom isn't saved. Every window opens at 42 points per second again, and an agent has no tool to set it.
52	
53	## Scroll the timeline
54	
55	Scroll, or swipe with two fingers, over the timeline. The track headers stay at the left and the ruler stays at the top while the lanes move.
56	
57	The timeline keeps 260 points of empty room past the last clip, so you can reach the end and drag a clip beyond it.
58	
59	The view also moves by itself to keep the playhead in sight. See [The ruler and playhead](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/).
60

68	title: "Select clips"
69	description: "Pick the clips you want to work on by clicking, dragging a marquee, or choosing a whole track or everything after the playhead."
70	---
71	
72	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
73	
74	The selection tells Frame Job which clips you mean. The inspector, the handles on the canvas and the commands in the menus all work on it. Selecting a clip changes nothing in the project.
75	
76	<AtAGlance
77	  menu={['Edit ▸ Select All', 'Edit ▸ Select After Playhead', 'Edit ▸ Select All on Track']}
78	  keys={['⌘A', '⌥⌘A']}
79	  where={['Click, ⇧-click or drag on the timeline', '⌥-click a track header']}
80	  tools="set_selection"
81	/>
82	
83	## Click a clip
84	
85	Click a clip to select it alone. It gets an outline, and the timeline bar names it.
86	
87	Clicking a clip that's already part of a larger selection keeps the whole selection, so you can drag the clips together. To get down to one clip, click empty space first, then click the clip.
88	
89	You can click a clip on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) to select it and read it in the inspector, but you can't drag or trim it.
90	
91	A double-click goes further: it [renames the clip](/timeline/names-and-labels/), or goes inside a [nest](/editing/nests/).
92	
93	## Add or remove a clip
94	
95	<kbd>⇧</kbd>-click a clip to add it to the selection. <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click a selected clip to take it out.
96	
97	## Drag a marquee
98	
99	Drag from any empty part of the timeline: a gap in a lane, the strip under the ruler, or the space below the last lane. A band follows the pointer and selects every clip it touches, however little of the clip it covers.
100	
101	- A plain drag replaces the selection.
102	- <kbd>⇧</kbd>-drag adds to the selection. Clips already selected stay selected.
103	- Clips on locked tracks are skipped.
104	
105	## Clear the selection
106	
107	Click an empty part of a lane, or the space above or below the lanes.
108	
109	:::caution
110	A double-click in an empty part of a lane [closes that gap](/editing/close-gaps/). That's an edit, not a deselect. Press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> if you did it by accident.
111	:::
112	
113	## Select all the clips
114	
115	**Edit ▸ Select All** (<kbd>⌘A</kbd>) selects every clip in the timeline you're editing, on locked tracks too. With a nest open, it selects the clips inside the nest.
116	
117	While you're typing in a field, <kbd>⌘A</kbd> selects the field's text instead. With the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-keys/)'s text in focus, it selects the words.
118	
119	## Select everything after the playhead
120	
121	**Edit ▸ Select After Playhead** (<kbd>⌥⌘A</kbd>) selects every clip whose start is at or after the playhead, on every track, including locked ones. A clip the playhead is partway through isn't included.
122	
123	Use it to push the rest of a project along: select everything after the playhead, then [drag it to make room](/editing/close-gaps/#open-room-by-hand).
124	
125	## Select all the clips on a track
126	
127	<kbd>⌥</kbd>-click a track's header to select every clip on that track, locked or not. On an empty track, this leaves nothing selected.
128	
129	**Edit ▸ Select All on Track** does the same for the current track, which is the track of the first selected clip, or the [front track](/timeline/tracks/) (the top lane) when nothing is selected. It's dimmed when the timeline has no clips, and it beeps when the current track is empty.
130	
131	## See what's selected
132	
133	The left end of the timeline bar names the selection.
134	
135	| Selected | The bar shows |
136	| --- | --- |
137	| One clip | A chip in the colour of the clip's kind (video, audio, text and so on), the clip's name, and its track and kind under it, such as `Track 2 · video` |
138	| Several clips | A count such as `3 clips`, over the track (or `2 tracks`) and the kind (or `mixed`) |
139	| Nothing | `No selection` |
140	
141	This block is a fixed width, so a long name is cut short and the tools beside it never move.
142	
143	## How a selection behaves
144	
145	A selection isn't an edit. It's never an undo step, it doesn't mark the project as changed, and it isn't saved, so a project always opens with nothing selected.
146	
147	- Selecting clips, on the timeline or with the Edit menu's commands, switches the inspector from the **Media** or **Document** tab to its **Clip** tab. The **Transcript** tab stays where it is.
148	- The timeline and the canvas share one selection. See [Select on the canvas](/canvas/select-on-canvas/).
149	- A clip that's deleted drops out of the selection.
150	- Going into a nest or coming back out changes the selection, because the clips on show are different.
151	
152	## With an agent
153	
154	[`set_selection`](/mcp/tools-view-state/#set_selection) sets the selection, and with no clips it clears it. An agent doesn't need it to edit, because its tools name their own clips. It matters for what depends on the selection, such as the canvas handles and the inspector. With a nest open, it selects inside the nest. See [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/).
155

163	title: "Snapping"
164	description: "Make timeline drags catch clip edges, markers, the playhead and the in and out points, and turn it off when you don't want it."
165	---
166	
167	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
168	
169	Snapping makes a drag catch the useful points on the timeline, so a clip lines up with the next cut instead of landing a frame away from it. This page is about the timeline. For dragging on the picture, see [Canvas snapping](/canvas/canvas-snapping/).
170	
171	<AtAGlance
172	  menu="View ▸ Snapping"
173	  keys="N"
174	  where="The Snap checkbox in the timeline bar"
175	/>
176	
177	## Turn snapping on or off
178	
179	Press <kbd>N</kbd>, click the **Snap** checkbox in the timeline bar, or choose **View ▸ Snapping**, which has a tick when snapping is on. The menu item shows no key, because <kbd>N</kbd> is one of the keys the editor handles itself.
180	
181	Snapping is on by default, and your choice is remembered between launches. One setting serves both the timeline and the canvas. There's no agent tool for it.
182	
183	## What a drag snaps to
184	
185	These drags snap:
186	
187	- moving clips
188	- trimming a clip's edge
189	- a [rate stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/)
190	- a [roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/)
191	- dragging a [marker](/timeline/markers/)
192	- scrubbing along the [ruler](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/)
193	
194	They catch these targets:
195	
196	- the start and the end of the timeline
197	- the edges of other clips, but never of the clips you're dragging
198	- markers
199	- the playhead
200	- the in and out points
201	
202	A target catches when it's within 8 points on screen, the unit macOS measures the screen in. That's the same distance at every zoom, so when you're zoomed out it covers more time. If two targets are equally close, the earlier one wins.
203	
204	When you move clips, it's the start of the earliest clip you're dragging that snaps, and the whole group moves with it. The end of a moved clip doesn't catch anything.
205	
206	Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), there are no markers to catch, and the other targets are the nest's own.
207	
208	## Turn snapping off for one drag
209	
210	Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> during the drag. It works from the moment you press or at any time during the drag, and it takes effect the next time the pointer moves. Let go of <kbd>⌘</kbd> and the drag snaps again.
211	
212	This works on the canvas too, and it changes nothing that's remembered.
213	
214	## See what a drag caught
215	
216	When a drag snaps, a thin vertical line runs across the timeline at the target it caught. Scrubbing the ruler snaps too, but it draws no line. The playhead is already there to show you.
217	
218	## Drags land on whole frames
219	
220	A drag that doesn't snap still lands on a whole frame. That's true with snapping off, while you're holding <kbd>⌘</kbd>, and when nothing is close enough to catch.
221	
222	## What never snaps
223	
224	- A [slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/) never snaps.
225	- A row from the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) dropped on a lane lands on the nearest frame at the pointer, and doesn't snap to edges.
226	- Dragging an [action band](/motion/action-lane/) lands on whole frames, and doesn't snap.
227	- Dragging a [fade handle](/audio/fades/) doesn't snap.
228	
229	## Good to know
230	
231	A window reads the setting when it opens. If two projects are open, changing it in one leaves the other as it is until you close that project and open it again.
232

241	title: Markers
242	description: Flag moments on the timeline, name them, jump between them, and turn them into chapters in an exported movie.
243	---
244	
245	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
246	
247	A marker is a flag on the ruler that remembers a moment in the project: a beat to cut on, a line to come back to, the start of a chapter.
248	
249	<AtAGlance
250	  menu={['Mark ▸ Add Marker', 'Mark ▸ Next Marker', 'Mark ▸ Previous Marker']}
251	  keys="M"
252	  where={['The bookmark button in the timeline bar', 'Document tab ▸ Markers']}
253	  tools={['add_marker', 'set_marker', 'remove_marker']}
254	/>
255	
256	## Add a marker
257	
258	Move the playhead to the moment and press <kbd>M</kbd>. The bookmark button in the timeline bar and **Mark ▸ Add Marker** do the same. <kbd>M</kbd> is a [single-letter key](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/), so the menu shows no shortcut beside the item, and it doesn't fire while you're typing in a field.
259	
260	A new marker is red and is called `Marker 1`, `Marker 2` and so on. Markers sit on whole frames, and two can't share one, so pressing <kbd>M</kbd> on a frame that already has one adds nothing and shows an alert saying a marker is already there.
261	
262	A marker draws on the ruler as a small flag with a thin line down the ruler, in its colour. An ordinary marker's flag is an outline, and a [chapter](#make-a-chapter) marker's is filled. A project can hold up to 1,024 markers.
263	
264	## Move, rename and remove a marker
265	
266	| To | Do this |
267	| --- | --- |
268	| Move a marker | Drag its flag along the ruler. You can grab it within 6 points of its line. It snaps as the playhead does, and it won't land on a frame that already has a marker. |
269	| Rename a marker | Double-click its flag, or type in its row in the Document tab. |
270	| Remove a marker | Choose **Delete** in its row in the Document tab. |
271	
272	Each of these is one undo step: **Move Marker**, **Rename Marker** or **Remove Marker**.
273	
274	Double-clicking a flag opens a field on the ruler. Return, Tab or a click elsewhere saves the name. <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the field and keeps the old name, and saving an empty field does nothing. The name field in the Document tab is different: empty it and the marker has no name, and the field shows **Marker** in grey.
275	
276	## Jump between markers
277	
278	**Mark ▸ Next Marker** and **Mark ▸ Previous Marker** pause playback and move the playhead to the marker. Neither has a keyboard shortcut. They beep when there's no marker further in that direction, and they're dimmed when the project has no markers.
279	
280	You can also choose **Go** in a marker's row in the Document tab.
281	
282	## The Markers list
283	
284	The **Markers** section of the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/) lists every marker in time order, with its time, its name, **Chapter**, **Go** and **Delete**. With no markers it reads "No markers. Press M to add one."
285	
286	## Make a chapter
287	
288	Tick **Chapter** in a marker's row, and its flag fills. It's one undo step, **Chapter Marker**, and unticking the box makes it an ordinary marker again.
289	
290	Chapter markers become chapters in exported MP4, MOV, M4A and WebM files, in time order. A chapter takes the marker's name, or "Chapter 1", "Chapter 2" and so on when the marker has no name. See [Chapters](/export/chapters/) for how a range export treats them.
291	
292	## Marker colours
293	
294	Markers are red unless an agent changes them, because a colour can only be set with `add_marker` or `set_marker`. The Document tab has no colour control. The colours are names, not hex values: `red`, `orange`, `yellow`, `green`, `blue` and `purple`, the same six as [clip labels](/timeline/names-and-labels/#colour-labels). Any other name draws the marker in the neutral text colour.
295	
296	## Good to know
297	
298	Markers belong to the whole timeline, and a nest has none of its own. While a [nest](/editing/nests/) is open:
299	
300	- The ruler shows no markers, and drags don't snap to them.
301	- The three marker commands in the **Mark** menu are off, and pressing <kbd>M</kbd> beeps.
302	- **Go** is disabled, because the playhead inside a nest counts from the nest's own start. Leave the nest with <kbd>⌘↑</kbd> to use it.
303	- The Document tab's list still shows every marker, and its name field, **Chapter** and **Delete** still work.
304	
305	## With an agent
306	
307	[`add_marker`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#add_marker) adds a marker at the playhead or at a time you give it, with its name, colour and chapter setting in the same call. [`set_marker`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#set_marker) moves a marker or changes any of those, and anything you leave out keeps its value. [`remove_marker`](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#remove_marker) removes one. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/).
308	
309	An agent works to the same rule as you do inside a nest. With a nest open it can't add a marker or move one, but it can rename one, change its colour or chapter setting, or remove it. Sending any of the three with an explicit `scope` fails, because a nest has no markers. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
310	
311	## Related

317	---
318	title: "The in/out range"
319	description: Mark a span of the timeline with I and O, so Loop, deletes, exports and other commands work on that passage alone.
320	---
321	
322	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
323	
324	The in/out range marks one passage of the timeline. Set it when you want to loop a section, cut it out, export it on its own, or point another command at it.
325	
326	<AtAGlance
327	  menu={['Mark ▸ Set In', 'Mark ▸ Set Out', 'Mark ▸ Clear Range']}
328	  keys={['I', 'O', '⌥X']}
329	  where="Shaded across the timeline's ruler and lanes"
330	  tools="set_range"
331	/>
332	
333	## Set In
334	
335	Move the playhead to where the passage starts and press <kbd>I</kbd>, or choose **Mark ▸ Set In**. With no range yet, the out point goes to the end of the timeline, so the range runs from the playhead to the end.
336	
337	## Set Out
338	
339	Move the playhead to where the passage ends and press <kbd>O</kbd>, or choose **Mark ▸ Set Out**. With no range yet, the in point goes to the start of the timeline.
340	
341	<kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd> are single-letter keys, so the menu shows no shortcut beside them, and they don't fire while you're typing in a field. See [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/).
342	
343	## Clear Range
344	
345	Press <kbd>⌥X</kbd> or choose **Mark ▸ Clear Range**. The item is available only while a range is set.
346	
347	## What the range is
348	
349	The range is a span shaded across the ruler and the lanes. It changes nothing by itself. These commands read it:
350	
351	| Command | What it does with the range |
352	| --- | --- |
353	| [Loop](/timeline/loop/) | Plays the range over and over, instead of the whole timeline. |
354	| <kbd>⌫</kbd> and <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> | With no clip selected, [Lift or Ripple Delete](/editing/delete-clips/) the range. With nothing selected and no range, they beep. |
355	| [Speed ramp presets](/speed/make-a-ramp/) | Cover the range when it lies entirely inside the clip. |
356	| [**Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip**](/color/adjustment-clips/) | Covers the range. With no range it covers the selected clips, or the whole timeline. |
357	| [Export](/export/range/) | Writes only the range when you set **Range:** to **In/out range**. |
358	| [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) | Changes the speed of everything in the range. |
359	| [New Project from Range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) | Opens a new project made of the range. |
360	| [Generate Captions](/captions/generate-captions/) | Offers **In/out range** under **From**, which takes every clip that overlaps the range, whole. |
361	| [Switch by Speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/) | Works over the range. With no range it works over the selected angle clips. |
362	
363	Two other things set the range for you. Selecting words in the [Transcript tab](/captions/delete-words/) makes them the range, and clearing that selection clears it. **Preview** for a [motion preset](/motion/motion-presets/) sets the range to the clip and turns Loop on, and both stay until you clear them.
364	
365	## Crossing points
366	
367	Setting an in point after the out point moves the out point to match, and setting an out point before the in point moves the in point. Both points then sit on the playhead, which is a range of no length, until you set the other end.
368	
369	A range of no length isn't shaded, and Loop plays the whole timeline. <kbd>⌫</kbd> and <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> treat it as no range at all, and the export sheet doesn't offer it. **Mark ▸ Clear Range** still clears it.
370	
371	## The range isn't saved
372	
373	The range belongs to the window you're working in, not to the project:
374	
375	- Setting or clearing it isn't an undo step, and it doesn't mark the project as edited.
376	- It isn't saved, so a project always opens with no range.
377	- It clears when you enter or leave a [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/), because a nest's time counts from its own start.
378	
379	## Good to know
380	
381	- Edits don't move the range. It stays at the same times while the clips under it change. After <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> on a range, the range is still there and now covers what moved up into it, so a second <kbd>⌘⌫</kbd> cuts again. Cutting words in the Transcript tab is the exception, and clears the range.
382	- Inside a nest you can set a range for Loop, deleting and **Retime Range**, but not for an export. The export sheet's **Range:** stays on **Whole project**, and its tooltip explains that the range belongs to the nest. **New Project from Range** is off while a nest is open.
383	
384	## With an agent
385	
386	[`set_range`](/mcp/tools-view-state/#set_range) sets either end or both, and clears the range when called with neither. Given one end, the other keeps its value, or falls back to the start or the end of the project when there's no range yet. Unlike Set In and Set Out, it won't move the other point for you, so an end at or before the start is an error.
387	
388	[`get_project`](/mcp/get-project/) reports the range as `in_out_range`, and [`export`](/mcp/tools-render-and-export/#export) with `range` set to `in_out` writes only that span. See [Tools: playhead, range and selection](/mcp/tools-view-state/).
389	
390	## Related
391

393	- [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/)
394	- [Export a range](/export/range/)
395	- [Markers](/timeline/markers/)
396	---
397	title: "Clip names and labels"
398	description: Give a clip its own name, clear it again, and mark clips with a colour label so a busy timeline is easier to read.
399	---
400	
401	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
402	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
403	
404	A name says what a clip is, and a colour label sorts it. Both help you find your way around a busy timeline.
405	
406	<AtAGlance
407	  menu={['Clip ▸ Rename…', 'Clip ▸ Label']}
408	  keys="⇧⌘R"
409	  where={['Double-click a clip on the timeline', 'The name field at the top of the Clip tab']}
410	  tools="set_clip"
411	/>
412	
413	## Rename a clip
414	
415	<Steps>
416	
417	1. Double-click the clip on the timeline, or select it and press <kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd> (**Clip ▸ Rename…**). A field opens over its name strip, showing the name the strip shows. With **Clip ▸ Rename…**, the timeline scrolls the clip into view first if it needs to.
418	
419	2. Type the name.
420	
421	3. Press Return or Tab, or click elsewhere.
422	
423	</Steps>
424	
425	The new name is its own undo step, **Rename Clip**, even when the click that ended it also made an edit.
426	
427	<kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the field and keeps the old name, with no undo step. Saving an empty field or an unchanged name does nothing, so a field you opened by accident is harmless.
428	
429	**Clip ▸ Rename…** is available when something is selected. With several clips selected, it opens the field on the first of them in timeline order. Spaces at either end of a name are trimmed.
430	
431	Double-clicking a nest clip opens the nest instead of renaming it. To rename a nest clip, select it and press <kbd>⇧⌘R</kbd>, or use the name field in the [Clip tab](#clear-a-name).
432	
433	## What a clip shows with no name
434	
435	A clip with no name of its own shows what it holds:
436	
437	| Clip | Shows |
438	| --- | --- |
439	| A nest | The nest's name |
440	| A clip from a file | The file's name |
441	| Text | Its words, or `Text` when it has none |
442	| A shape | The kind of shape |
443	| A graphic | `Graphic` |
444	| An adjustment clip | `Adjustment` |
445	
446	## Clear a name
447	
448	The name field at the top of the [Clip tab](/getting-started/inspector/) names one clip. Empty it to clear the clip's name and go back to what the clip holds. This is the only place you can clear a name, because the field on the timeline ignores an empty name.
449	
450	The field also renames the clip when you type in it, and either way it's one undo step, **Rename Clip**. It appears only with a single clip selected. With several selected, the header reads how many, for example "3 clips selected".
451	
452	## Colour labels
453	
454	<Steps>
455	
456	1. Select the clips.
457	
458	2. Choose a colour from **Clip ▸ Label**: **Red**, **Orange**, **Yellow**, **Green**, **Blue** or **Purple**. Choose **None** to remove a label.
459	
460	</Steps>
461	
462	A label applies to every selected clip as one undo step, **Label Clip**. Labels are for your own sorting, and they don't change how a clip plays or exports.
463	
464	A labelled clip has a small dot in its colour at the right end of its name strip. On a clip too narrow to fit both, the strip keeps its kind symbol and drops the dot. See [Reading a clip](/timeline/reading-a-clip/).
465	
466	The menu is available when something is selected. It checks a colour when every selected clip has that label, and **None** when none has a label. Choosing a label every selected clip already has beeps and changes nothing.
467	
468	The [Clip tab](/getting-started/inspector/)'s header shows the dot at the end of the name line when every selected clip has the same label. There's no dot when they differ or none has one.
469	
470	## Good to know
471	
472	- A clip on a locked track can still be renamed, because a lock protects a clip's place on the timeline, and a name isn't placement.
473	- Split, duplicate, detach and paste carry a clip's name and label to the new clip. [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) never does.
474	- The field stays open through a zoom or a change an agent makes. If the clip is deleted while the field is open, the field closes and what you typed is dropped.
475	- The same field renames [tracks](/timeline/manage-tracks/) and [markers](/timeline/markers/).
476	
477	## With an agent
478	
479	`set_clip` names or labels several clips in one step, where a person names one at a time. A name or label you leave out stays as it is, and null or an empty string clears it. It stores any label it's given, and one outside the six colours draws in the neutral text colour, so keep to the six. See [Tools: text, shapes and clip names](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/#set_clip).
480	
481	## Related
482	
483	- [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/)
484	- [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/)
485	- [Markers](/timeline/markers/)
486	---
487	title: "The preview"
488	description: What the preview pane shows, what its corner tags mean, and the View menu items that change it.
489	---
490	
491	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
492	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
493	
494	The preview shows the frame under the playhead, so you can see what you're making while you edit and play.
495	
496	<AtAGlance
497	  menu={['View ▸ Safe Areas', 'View ▸ Show Ungraded', 'View ▸ Show Selection', 'View ▸ Show SDR Version', 'View ▸ Show Subjects', 'View ▸ Scopes', 'View ▸ Loudness Meter']}
498	  keys={['⌃⌘U', '⌃⌘W', '⌃⌘L']}
499	  where="The editor window, top left, above the timeline"
500	/>
501	
502	## What it shows
503	
504	The picture keeps the canvas's shape, letterboxed to fit the pane to the left of the inspector. Under it, a small caption gives the canvas size and frame rate, for example `1920 × 1080 · 30 fps`.
505	
506	The preview is also where you work on the picture: selecting clips, then moving, scaling, rotating and cropping them. That's covered in [The canvas](/canvas/the-canvas/), and zooming it in [Zoom and pan the preview](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/).
507	
508	Two settings change how the preview is drawn, and neither touches an export:
509	
510	- [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/) draws it smaller, so heavy projects play more smoothly.
511	- [The Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/) shows the same picture in a second window, for another display.
512	
513	## Preview tags
514	
515	Small tags in the top-left corner of the pane tell you when the picture isn't the plain one. Each shows only while its **View** item is on.
516	
517	| Tag | Means | View item |
518	| --- | --- | --- |
519	| **Ungraded** | The picture shows no clip's grade. | [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/) |
520	| **Selection** | The picture shows which pixels the selected adjustment clip's qualifier picks. | [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) |
521	| **SDR Version** | The picture shows the project's SDR version. | [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/) |
522	
523	<Shot
524	  name="04b-preview-scopes.preview"
525	  alt="The preview pane with the Ungraded tag in its top-left corner, the picture with its caption 960 × 540 · 30 fps underneath, and the scopes panel beside it showing a waveform over a vectorscope."
526	/>
527	
528	The tags sit in that order, and a hidden tag leaves no space, so **Selection** moves into the corner when **Ungraded** is off. **SDR Version** shows in an SDR project too, where the picture doesn't change.
529	
530	## Other View items
531	
532	The **View** menu holds the other switches for the preview. Each has its own page.
533	
534	| Item | Keys | What it does | Remembered |
535	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
536	| [**Safe Areas**](/canvas/safe-areas/) | | Shows the title-safe and action-safe guides, the same as the toolbar's **Safe** box. Checked when on. | Yes |
537	| [**Show Ungraded**](/color/show-ungraded/) | <kbd>⌃⌘U</kbd> | Shows the picture as if no clip were graded. | No |
538	| [**Show Selection**](/color/show-selection/) | | Shows what an adjustment clip's qualifier picks. It needs a selected adjustment clip to turn on. | No |
539	| [**Show SDR Version**](/hdr/show-sdr-version/) | | Shows an HDR project's SDR version. | No |
540	| [**Show Subjects**](/framing/show-subjects/) | | Draws the faces, people and salient regions found for the selected clip. | No |
541	| [**Scopes**](/color/scopes/) | <kbd>⌃⌘W</kbd> | Shows the scopes panel beside the picture. | No |
542	| [**Loudness Meter**](/audio/loudness-meter/) | <kbd>⌃⌘L</kbd> | Shows the live loudness column beside the picture. | No |
543	
544	Remembered means between launches, for every project. The items that aren't remembered start off in each new window, as the [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/) does, and none of these changes an export.
545	
546	**View ▸ Assistant** (<kbd>⌃⌘A</kbd>) sits nearby but doesn't change the picture. It opens the inspector's Assistant tab, beside the preview. See [Chat with the Assistant](/assistant/chat/).
547	
548	## Related
549	
550	- [A tour of the editor window](/getting-started/editor-window/)

554	---
555	title: "Preview Quality"
556	description: Draw the preview at half or a quarter of the canvas size so a heavy project plays more smoothly, without changing what you export.
557	---
558	
559	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
560	
561	Preview Quality draws the preview smaller and scales it back up to fit, so a heavy project plays more smoothly. It never changes an export.
562	
563	<AtAGlance menu="View ▸ Preview Quality" />
564	
565	## Full, Half, Quarter
566	
567	Choose **View ▸ Preview Quality ▸ Full**, **Half** or **Quarter**. The menu checks the current choice. The preview redraws straight away, paused or playing.
568	
569	| Choice | Draws the preview at | 1920 × 1080 canvas |
570	| --- | --- | --- |
571	| **Full** (default) | The canvas size | 1920 × 1080 |
572	| **Half** | Half the width and height | 960 × 540 |
573	| **Quarter** | A quarter of the width and height | 480 × 270 |
574	
575	The choice is remembered between launches, for every project. There's no keyboard shortcut, and no agent tool sets it. The [Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/) shows the same picture, so it draws at the same quality.
576	
577	## What it changes
578	
579	Quality only affects the preview. It never changes an export, a [saved frame](/export/save-frame/) or a frame an agent renders.
580	
581	A lower choice saves the work of drawing each pixel of the picture. Decoding your footage, drawing shadows and playing the sound cost the same at every choice, so a project held back by those won't speed up as much.
582	
583	## Good to know
584	
585	The picture always keeps the canvas's exact shape, so that handles stay in the right place on it. On an awkward canvas size that means the preview can draw a little larger than the fraction, never smaller:
586	
587	| Canvas | Half | Quarter |
588	| --- | --- | --- |
589	| 999 × 666 | 501 × 334 | 252 × 168 |
590	| 1001 × 667 | 1001 × 667 | 1001 × 667 |
591	
592	A canvas whose sides share no common factor, like 1001 × 667, can't be scaled down evenly, so it draws at full size at every choice.
593	
594	## Related
595	
596	- [The preview](/timeline/preview/)
597	- [The Preview Window](/timeline/preview-window/)
598	- [Play, pause and shuttle](/timeline/playback/)
599	---
600	title: "The Preview Window"
601	description: Show the picture in a second window with no handles or guides, on another display or full screen.
602	---
603	
604	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
605	
606	The Preview Window shows the picture on its own, with no handles or guides over it. Use it to put the picture on a second display while you edit in the main window.
607	
608	<AtAGlance menu="View ▸ Preview Window" keys="⇧⌘P" />
609	
610	## Open the Preview Window
611	
612	Press <kbd>⇧⌘P</kbd> or choose **View ▸ Preview Window**. The same key hides it again, and the menu item has a checkmark while it's open. It opens on an empty timeline too, where the window is black.
613	
614	The window is titled after the project, for example "Intro — Preview", and has a black surround. You can resize it down to 320 × 200, and it can go full screen.
615	
616	It uses the same player as the main preview, so the two never drift apart. [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/), **Show Ungraded**, **Show Selection** and **Show SDR Version** all apply to it, but the [corner tags](/timeline/preview/#preview-tags) don't appear in it.
617	
618	The window is only for looking. Safe-area guides, zoom and the handles for moving clips stay in the main preview.
619	
620	## Remembered position
621	
622	The window remembers its position and size between launches, so it opens where you last left it, on a second display for example. The first time, it opens at 640 × 360 in the middle of the screen. It stays visible when you switch to another app.
623	
624	It closes with its project window. Whether it's open isn't remembered, so it starts off in each new window.
625	
626	## Keys
627	
628	The window doesn't take you away from the editor. While it has the focus:
629	
630	- Playback keys work: <kbd>Space</kbd>, <kbd>J</kbd>, <kbd>K</kbd>, <kbd>L</kbd>, the arrows, Home and End.
631	- The editor's other single-letter keys work too, such as <kbd>M</kbd> for a marker or <kbd>I</kbd> and <kbd>O</kbd> for the range.
632	- Every editor ⌘ command works, so <kbd>⌘E</kbd> opens the export sheet and <kbd>⌘T</kbd> splits.
633	- <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> undoes the project's last step, and <kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd> redoes it, the same steps as in the editor.
634	- <kbd>⌘W</kbd> closes the Preview Window, not the project.
635	
636	Single-letter keys stop while a field in the editor window is being edited, or while the editor has a sheet open.
637	
638	## Good to know
639	
640	- There's one saved position for every project. With two projects' Preview Windows open at once, the second opens on top of the first, and only one of them saves where it's moved to.
641	- The window isn't listed in the **Window** menu. Use **View ▸ Preview Window** to find it.
642	- After you save a project under a new name, the title updates the next time you show the window.
643
